Before @UUID[JournalEntry.w9xeQJg6psfiMjFU.JournalEntryPage.yyXMKcpDOIhGuZIB]{A0-E01 · The Call from SAFE}, each PC lives through a brief moment in the small hours of the same night as the break-in. These are one- or two-minute scenes, with no tests, so that every player starts the game with something in hand. Read them separately or together.

Storyteller Notes · Preludes

Celeste (@UUID[JournalEntry.zQMt8VMfKPoL6INq]{PJ-02}). At 3:30 a.m., @UUID[Actor.eRE6FTNdGO76lzPK]{Mr. Pell} texts her asking her to authorize “an urgent payment to a security vendor” from one of Halloway Meridian's companies. It's routine. She signs off on it. (It's the payment to the @UUID[Actor.9rv5Jdb3y6bZZ1fj]{MEN-01} crew. If she reviews the transfer later, it's a clue: , early.)

Ezra (@UUID[JournalEntry.PBJeE9T9n0BjB6ag]{PJ-03}). On his monitors underground, at 2:52 a.m., a block of doorbell cameras in Ballard goes dark. All Gale Sentinel, all at once, for eleven minutes. He's never seen an outage that clean. (.)

Nadia (@UUID[JournalEntry.rg50DlMYSzgbZeBv]{PJ-04}). At 3:20 a.m. she gets a voicemail from @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen} on her regular phone. Just four seconds of breathing, then it cuts off. (Helen started to call her and hung up. Nadia can go to the apartment on her own.)

Hal (@UUID[JournalEntry.B4nqUk8dojvCw97H]{PJ-05}). He's watching David's hangar on @UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Montgomery}'s orders, as he does every few weeks. At 3:21 a.m. he sees David and @UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Bear} tear out in the truck. (Hal can follow them or report in.)

Ruth (@UUID[JournalEntry.gRfqeOIXEHOcLemr]{PJ-06}). She's on leave, at home, unable to sleep. At 3:40 a.m. her ex-husband, the retired detective, calls her: “They tell me there's a weird call in Ballard nobody wants to take. You know anything?” (She doesn't know anything yet. But she will.)

Editor's Note · Celeste's Clue

Installment 1 (doc 10) called this clue “P-11, early.” Installment 2 (doc 11) defines P-14 as the payment to Lonnie “made from Cascade Holdings LLC, a Halloway Meridian company (the one Celeste signed in her prelude),” and Part 4 (doc 13) refers to “P-14 and the prelude note.” The newest doc wins: it's @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.9WkqebVXUF2scLLC]{The Payment from Cascade Holdings}. P-11 is still the Gale signature (@UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center}).

Storyteller Context

It's 3:19 a.m. @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David}'s flip phone rings for the first time in four years. The conversation is the one told in @UUID[JournalEntry.CeLqLZCfHQEtHYlk]{CAP-00}. Fifteen minutes later, David and @UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Bear} reach @UUID[JournalEntry.YD0Td8Y9aJyIpGSl]{Helen's apartment}. David doesn't go alone: from the truck, he calls in the coterie. He calls whoever's close at hand and tells them where, not why.

  • Nadia arrives on her own if she followed up on her prelude: she knows the apartment.
  • Hal arrives behind the truck, or because David calls him.
  • Ezra and Ruth already have Ballard on their minds from their preludes. If David calls them, they come.
  • Celeste arrives only if the table agreed on how she knows David (see “Character Tips” in @UUID[JournalEntry.ll97TEj4MRjtM595]{Chapter 7 · The Ward File}). If not, she joins in @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.T8gJWjZpOnL4OisP]{A1-E01 · What They Took} or @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.xWx5IoPih8fX83b1]{A1-E03 · The Sheriff Asks}.

Those who don't arrive tonight meet up in @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.xWx5IoPih8fX83b1]{A1-E03 · The Sheriff Asks}.

The goal of the scene is simple: secure @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen}, figure out what happened, and get out of there before things get worse. What the coterie doesn't know is that the doorbell camera of 3B, across from Helen's door, is still streaming.

Market Street gleams in the rain. The hardware store is closed, its shutter rolled down, and above it, on the third floor, a single window is lit. The street door is open. The stairwell smells of damp, of wet wool, and of something else, metallic and sweet, like coins squeezed in a fist. In the third-floor hallway every door has a doorbell camera, each with its little blue light. Helen's door is closed. From the other side, someone is counting under their breath: “...one hundred forty-one, one hundred forty-two...”

Tests

  • Wits + Awareness (Difficulty 3): the 3B doorbell camera, the only one in the hallway pointed at Helen's door, has a steady blue light and a second, tiny green light, blinking. It's streaming live.
  • Resolve + Awareness (Difficulty 2), or automatic with Auspex 1: the coin smell in the hallway is Vitae, but watered down and with no Beast behind it. It's a ghoul's ().
  • Intelligence + Technology (Difficulty 3): the cameras on her door and the one on 3B are the same Gale Sentinel model. Helen's has a disconnection log from 2:52 to 3:03 ().

Coterie Options

Escape Taking Helen down the fire escape avoids the 3B camera. Dexterity + Stealth (Difficulty 2) so nobody in the building sees them go down. If they leave through the hallway without doing anything about the camera, ANOMALY logs each Kindred as a “cold subject”: .
Manipulate Helen is in shock and only half trusts David, who's the only one she called. One PC talks her into it: Charisma + Persuasion (Difficulty 2) to get her to agree to leave with them tonight; if David backs up the speaker, +1 die. On a failure, she refuses to leave her home until dawn. With 3 or more successes, she volunteers the business about the ghoul who sniffed the stairwell.
Combat There's nobody to fight. But if someone smashes the 3B camera, the last image it sends is a hand moving faster than it should (). Opening it carefully and disconnecting it is Dexterity + Larceny (Difficulty 3), and the Thermometer doesn't rise.
Disciplines Obfuscate (Cloak of Shadows) keeps the camera from recording whoever uses it, but not the others. Auspex 4 (Spirit's Touch) on the doorknob: gloves, a calm pulse, and a thirst for something that isn't food, the mark of a ghoul waiting for their next fix (). Dominate on Helen to calm her down works, but Helen notices the gap in her memory the next day. Helen is David's Touchstone: if he sees it, he steps in (“Not her.”). If they do it anyway, until @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.xWx5IoPih8fX83b1]{A1-E03 · The Sheriff Asks} he does nothing to help whoever dominated her.

Dialogue Guide: Helen Ward

Helen is exhausted and scared, but she's still a journalist. She talks fast, smokes, and asks questions the moment she can. With David she's more direct than with anyone.

  • “Are you okay?” — “I'm in one piece. Okay is something else.”
  • “What did they take?” — “Everything that matters. The drive, the copy in the closet. And somebody wiped the cloud at 3:01. This isn't some random burglar: they didn't even take the TV.”
  • “Who knew the file existed?” — “Nadia, my producer. My source at the M.E.'s office. You, I guess.” She looks at him. “Did you know?”
  • “Did you see their faces?” — “Caps, gloves. One of them stopped in the hallway and sniffed the stairwell. Like a dog. He smelled like wet wool and coins.”
  • (Asked by David, or by a PC who has already seen @UUID[JournalEntry.EQ3lkuiGnEvoSW7x]{DOC-05}) “Why didn't you change the lock?” — She looks at David. She's quiet for a moment. “Because you never told me why. And I don't do things without knowing why.”
  • “Who are they?” (to David, about the PCs who came with him) — “Don't take me for an idiot. I called one number and three people showed up. None of them blinks enough.”

Clues

(the cameras offline from 2:52 to 3:03) · (ghoul Vitae on the doorknob and in the hallway)

Exits

@UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.T8gJWjZpOnL4OisP]{A1-E01 · What They Took} (the scene continues in the apartment) · if the coterie takes Helen away right away, A1-E01 happens at the @UUID[JournalEntry.104UV0anmZHNCTrD]{hangar}, and P-02 is lost if it wasn't detected.

Storyteller Notes

  • If nobody notices the 3B camera, don't say so. Let it be a surprise in @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.wIpc0OR2nQf7WDFO]{A1-E05 · The City's Eyes} or @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center}, when they find their own image on Gale's servers.
  • David, in this scene: he wants Helen out of there, seeing as little as possible. He explains nothing, to her or to the coterie. If a PC asks him who SAFE is, he answers “Me” and nothing more.
  • Bear stays in the truck watching the street. If someone asks him, he saw a gray electric car parked half a block down with someone inside: it's the ghoul lookout (@UUID[Actor.BzNGxOAK3F6Uo56T]{MEN-04}). If the coterie does nothing, it leaves at 4:10.
